evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate (lines 1104-1116) only requires nonempty, differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs in the before/after snapshots. It never requires both observations to be from the same boot, even though the snapshot structure carries `boot_id` (the reboot check at 1117-1124 reads `before`/`after` `boot_id`, and both snapshot pairs are iterated together at 1143-1145). A guest reboot between the restart command returning and the second inspect produces a fresh manager with a new PID and invocation ID, so the check reports a manager restart even though the pair straddles a boot. Requiring nonempty, equal `boot_id` in the manager snapshot pair while keeping the PID/invocation checks is the smallest compatible correctness repair and does not change normal same-boot results.
